Divrei Neviïm ha-'Atidot Yad'u — reshut No1 from the Old Sefaradi Tiqun for Shabbat Divrei

tei:bibl.tei:title: דִּבְרֵי נְבִיאִים הָעֲתִידוֹת יָדְעוּ
Divrei Neviïm ha-'Atidot Yad'u — reshut No1 from the Old Sefaradi Tiqun for Shabbat Divrei
tei:bibl.tei:note: Converted from the export of opensiddur.org at 624215eef0.

tei:div.tei:p: In older Sephardic practice, there are cycles of reshuyot (permission-poems) recited on the three sabbaths of rebuke. These reshuyot, inserted before important prayers, date back to medieval Andalusian poets. They are largely mournful in tone, and accordingly the Ḥida opposed their recitation as unbefitting the joy of sabbaths, but due to their antiquity and cherishedness some communities (for instance those of Morocco) preserved them, reciting them all prior to Maariv on the ninth of Av instead. In any case, they are very clearly designed for the Shabbatot to which they are assigned, and to serve as reshuyot for the prayers to which they are assigned.

This is the first of six reshuyot for the first sabbath of rebuke, Shabbat Divrei, the first Sabbath of Rebuke after 17 Tammuz. It is the first reshut recited before Nishmat at the outset of the Shaḥarit service.
